feature: Money-path E2E (consolidates #886–891) — setup → create/execute → verify login → teardown, one self-contained account-lifecycle flow
notes: GIT #987 (Epic #803). This single manifest CONSOLIDATES the six money-path manifests — #886 assessment/home-quiz.json, #887 copilot-readiness/consent-scan-trigger.json, #888 copilot-readiness/verdict-pillars.json, #889 copilot-readiness/documents-screen.json, #890 copilot-readiness/sow-proposal.json, #891 copilot-readiness/checkout.json — into ONE create → use → verify → teardown lifecycle, restructuring the account lifecycle around every content/theme/honesty assertion those six already proved (none discarded; each is preserved and labelled with its origin issue below).

PHASE → EXECUTOR-BUCKET MAPPING (MainWindow.RunManifestAsync runs phases in a FIXED order: apiTests → graphTests → postGraphApiTests → zohoTests → uiSteps → powerShellVerify, all sharing ONE #877 TestRunVariables store so an extracted value flows forward into every later phase). Setup + Create + Execute(API) + Verify all live in `apiTests` (they must be strictly ordered and precede teardown). Teardown lives in `postGraphApiTests` — because graphTests is empty it runs immediately after apiTests, i.e. AFTER verify. The preserved UI content assertions live in `uiSteps`. Every step's `name` is prefixed with its phase (SETUP/CREATE/EXECUTE/VERIFY/TEARDOWN) so a failure names its phase straight from the live log: apiTests/postGraphApiTests log on the `testing.api-executor` channel, uiSteps on `testing.ui-executor`.

WHY TEARDOWN IS in postGraphApiTests, NOT after uiSteps: the executor has NO HTTP bucket after uiSteps (only powerShellVerify, which runs pwsh Get-* cmdlets, not arbitrary POSTs). So an HTTP teardown structurally cannot run after the UI assertions. This is safe here because the teardown is the CONSERVATIVE #986 reset (clears tenant_engine_overrides + the write-action audit log only) plus the rollback-endpoint contract check — it deletes NO account, scan run, verdict, document, or SOW that the uiSteps observe.

*** HONESTY CAVEAT — 'CREATE ITS OWN ACCOUNT' (the load-bearing constraint) ***: the platform mints the credentialed account (`users` row) ONLY inside the Microsoft admin-consent OAuth callback (`provisionProspectAccount`, direct-tenant-provisioning.ts), and only unlocks its password via `POST /api/public/flow/set-password` AFTER a real Stripe payment flips the checkout session to `paid`. Neither the interactive Microsoft admin-consent OAuth redirect nor a genuinely-confirmed Stripe PaymentIntent is drivable by BuildConsole's WebView2 + HTTP harness, and the harness has NO client-side unique-value generator (TestRunVariables only holds Settings config vars + values extracted from real responses — see TestRunVariables.cs). So a fully harness-minted, unique-per-run login credential is architecturally impossible past that consent+payment wall. What this flow DOES do, honestly: (a) CREATE — it drives the REAL public intake `POST /api/public/checkout-session` (the exact call the quiz→details step fires), minting a genuinely NEW checkout_sessions row + funnel lead every run, and asserts the new session resolves; (b) VERIFY — it performs a real `POST /api/auth/login` credential round-trip. The credentials it logs in with are the designated testbed Assessment account's (config vars), NOT a freshly-minted password — because minting one is impossible here. This is the honest maximum; fabricating an end-to-end account creation was explicitly NOT done. See PLATFORM_BUILD.md #987 row / the issue for Shane's sign-off on this boundary.

SCAN IS ASYNC + MAINTAINED-STATE ASSUMPTION: `POST /api/portal/assessment/debug-trigger-scan` returns 202 `{ runId, status:'pending' }` and runs `runDiagnostics` in the background; the executor cannot await its completion. The EXECUTE apiTests fire it to prove the real trigger contract (202 + a persisted active run + a backend-computed checksTotal — #887's honesty checks), but the verdict/pillars/documents/SOW assertions (API and UI) read the testbed Assessment account's MAINTAINED, already-completed scan — exactly as #888/#889/#890 already assumed. The deep `POST /api/portal/assessment/debug-reset-session` wipe (quiz + diagnostic runs + doc-gen + documents) is therefore DELIBERATELY NOT invoked inside this flow: wiping + async-re-triggering could not restore a completed verdict before the uiSteps run, and would leave every #888/#889 UI assertion asserting the unavailable state. Its contract is noted here for a future synchronous-scan-capable variant. Precondition: keep the testbed Assessment account in a scanned state (a completed scan with a verdict, ≥2 generated documents, and a resolvable SOW), same precondition #888–#890 already require.

GRAPH-WRITE TEARDOWN (#986 teardown-graph-writes): the money path performs NO M365 Graph WRITE actions — the live scan is read-only diagnostics; Launch Control write-actions/remediation are a SEPARATE flow (covered by copilot-readiness/remediation-tracker-e2e.json). So there is nothing real to roll back here. Rather than fabricate a write, the TEARDOWN step exercises the rollback endpoint's dev-origin gate + admin/ingest auth + independent-failure envelope with a deliberately OUT-OF-RANGE auditLogId (proving the path is reachable and gated, returning `toreDown:true` with that id recorded as failed, since rollbackExecution never aborts the batch). A future variant that adds a real write-action captures that write's `/execute` auditLogId and passes it here NEWEST-FIRST (LIFO), per #986's contract.

STRIPE / CHECKOUT (from #891): the journey-checkout HAPPY path (Stripe's own hosted card page) and the signed-scope precondition (`cj_signed_scope` in sessionStorage, set only by Screen 3's drawn-canvas signature) are NOT executor-drivable (WebView2+JS-injection cannot seed sessionStorage, draw the signature, or wait for the cross-origin Stripe redirect). Preserved here is #891's fully-runnable NEGATIVE honesty guardrail: on the checkout route with no signed scope, the 'no signed scope' panel is visible and the pay button is absent (the 2401cbe7 guardrail). Because this session never signs a scope, that negative state is the natural, real observation. Stripe is in TEST mode for any .replit.dev origin (stripe.ts getStripeKey → sk_test_), so nothing here can ever touch a live key.

MUTUALLY-EXCLUSIVE POINT-IN-TIME UI STATES (why some #887/#891 UI selectors are represented at the API level instead of as uiSteps): a single linear WebView2 session holds ONE point in time. #887's live-scan OVERLAY (cj-scan-overlay / cj-scan-streaming-label / cj-scan-checks-done) is only visible DURING an in-progress scan, which is mutually exclusive with the COMPLETED-verdict state #888/#889/#890 need — so #887's Scene-0 honesty contract is preserved via its API assertions in EXECUTE (consentStatus granted, 202 trigger, active.runId, active.checksTotal) and its overlay selectors stay covered by re-running a mid-scan snapshot. Likewise #891's signed-scope happy path is mutually exclusive with its own no-signed-scope negative case; the negative case is what runs here.

ENV VARS required in BuildConsole → Settings → Test Environment Variables: DEPLOY_URL (deployed origin serving both the marketing quiz at '/' and the portal at /login + /copilot-readiness — the same single origin all six source manifests targeted), SECRET_KEY (= BUILD_TRACKER_INGEST_TOKEN; the Bearer that satisfies requireAdminOrIngestToken on the #986 testbed endpoints and the #901 testbed-customers lookup, per requireAuth.ts), TEST_PORTAL_EMAIL / TEST_PORTAL_PASSWORD (the designated testbed Assessment account), TEST_PORTAL_SLUG (portal branding slug for the login route). The testbed customerId (tenants.id) is NOT a config var — it is read live from the DB via GET /api/admin/baseline-templates/testbed-customers (the same proven #901 bootstrap), so the reset always targets a real testbed customer, never a guessed literal.

The #986 testbed endpoints are hard-gated to a real .replit.dev dev origin (requireDevOrigin, reusing isReplitDevEnvironment from stripe.ts); against a real deployment they 403 by design. Run this manifest against the .replit.dev dev origin. No raw DB access is used anywhere here — every clean/reset/rollback goes through the gated endpoints, per #987.

postGraphApiTests.name: TEARDOWN 1/2 — Graph-write rollback (#986 teardown-graph-writes): exercise the endpoint's dev-origin gate + admin/ingest auth + independent-failure envelope. The money path makes NO real M365 Graph WRITE actions (read-only scan; Launch Control writes are the separate remediation flow), so this is driven with a deliberately out-of-range auditLogId to prove the rollback path is reachable and gated without fabricating a write; the batch records it as failed and still returns toreDown:true.
